topic: An Indiana man skipped the All-Star Game to share a widower's birthday cake for his late wife
title: He Skipped the All-Star Game for a Widower He'd Just Met #truestory
description:
#truestory #kindness #widower

"Looks like you've got a big night planned."

A dozen roses, a birthday cake, and a man in a wheelchair at the deli. His wife passed five years ago, and he still buys her a cake every birthday. A stranger skipped the All-Star Game to sit at his table.

#mayorofmainst #truestory #kindness

Source: FOX 13, CBS News (July 2018), Gregory Johnson's Facebook post

Retold with AI voice & visuals
fact_notes: FOX 13 (2018-07): Gregory Johnson, Kroger (Indianapolis area; CBS: Greenwood, Ind.), Tuesday of MLB All-Star Game (2018-07-17), teriyaki chicken breast, deli line, older man Jim in wheelchair, dozen roses + birthday cake, 'It looks like you've got a big night planned', 'saddest eyes', wife died 5 years ago, roses+cake every birthday; met Gloria in high school, he star basketball player, she cheerleader at rival school, his team beat hers in semi-finals, friend introduced, asked her to come back next night, her quote 'Furthermore, I don't even know you and I have much better things to do tomorrow night than watch your high school play again', stormed out with friends, next night sectional championship win, she showed up, stuck around to congratulate, together ever since; first house, children; loved her as much the day she passed as the day they married; about an hour; 'no way I was cutting this visit short over a silly baseball game.
